voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: In May of eighteen twenty-eight, a teenage boy appeared in a town square in Nuremberg, Germany. He could barely speak. In his hand, an unsigned letter — no name, no home, no past.
He learned to talk. Learned to write. And all of Europe began to whisper the same theory: that he was a stolen prince, hidden away since infancy to protect someone else's throne.
In 1829 someone attacked him with a knife; he survived. In December of 1833, someone lured him to a garden with the promise of a purse — and stabbed him for real. He died three days later.

In his purse, police found a note in mirror writing, from someone signing only M, L, period, O. It described Hauser precisely — and promised nothing else. His own epitaph reads: a riddle of his time. Birth unknown. Death mysterious.

For two hundred years, the prince theory held. Then in 2024, new DNA analysis ruled it out for good — his blood doesn't match the royal family it was supposed to hide. Which leaves everything else exactly where it started.
